title: Rank, Position and Height Ordering
shortDescription: Ranks from top and bottom, total counts, left/right positions and height/weight comparison arrangements.
genZNote: '12th from top' and '18th from bottom' sound like two different people — they're the same person. One formula, zero stress.

sections.heading: Rank Formulas
bullets: Total = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1.
Rank from bottom = total − rank from top + 1.
Persons between A and B (A ahead of B) = rank of B − rank of A − 1.
Position from left/right in a row: total = left position + right position − 1.
If two people swap places and rank changes, difference gives people between them.
Example: Ravi is 12th from top and 18th from bottom → total = 12 + 18 − 1 = 29.

sections.heading: Height and Order Comparisons
bullets: Write relations as a chain with symbols: A > B > C means A is taller than B who is taller than C.
Use ">" for "taller than", "<" for "shorter than"; combine statements sharing a common person.
Questions: who is tallest/shortest, who is in the middle, how many are taller than X.
Order of ranks in exams: rank from top counted from the highest scorer; "rank from last" counted from lowest.
If information is insufficient to compare two people directly, the answer is "cannot be determined".

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Five friends: P is taller than Q but shorter than R. S is taller than R but shorter than T. Order from tallest: T > S > R > P > Q. Shortest: Q; middle: R.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Rank problems rely on total = top + bottom − 1; height-ordering problems chain comparative statements into one sequence.
keyFacts: Chain A > B > C helps with comparisons.

highYieldFacts: Always add 1 back when converting between top and bottom ranks.
commonTraps: Do not count the two named persons among "between".

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)
